item.title: Freezing liquid inside optical fibre makes light and sound interact 1,000 times more strongly
item.description: Scientists have frozen the liquid inside a special optical fibre to -196°C, creating conditions where light and sound interact more than 1,000 times more strongly than in ordinary fibres. The team found that the frozen fibre could still guide light and hypersonic sound waves. The breakthrough also helped researchers demonstrate optoacoustic memory, which could have potential applications in lower-energy photonic computing, quantum information processing and high-precision sensing. item.title: Mexico brings back bison 160 years after extinction; 47 animals are restoring the ecosystem
item.description: After an absence of 160 years, American bison have made a remarkable comeback to Coahuila, Mexico. These majestic animals have become vital ecosystem engineers, actively rejuvenating worn-out landscapes. Their presence enhances soil quality and promotes water absorption in the dry terrain. Additionally, this return facilitates the resurgence of native predators and other wildlife, reflecting a wider initiative aimed at restoring vital species throughout North America.
